AboutPage.title: About Erasmus+
AboutPage.intro: Discover Erasmus+, the European Union programme that opens doors to international education, professional development, and cultural exchange.
AboutPage.whatText1: Erasmus+ is the European Union programme supporting education, training, youth, and sport in Europe. It provides opportunities for students, academic staff, and university employees to gain international experience.
AboutPage.whatText2: Through Erasmus+, participants can study, complete traineeships, teach, or receive training abroad. The programme promotes cooperation between institutions, develops professional and personal skills, and encourages cultural understanding.
AboutPage.periodText: The Erasmus+ programme for 2021–2027 focuses on inclusion and diversity, digital transformation, environmental sustainability, and participation in democratic life.
AboutPage.opportunitiesIntro: Erasmus+ offers different opportunities for students and university staff to develop their skills and gain valuable international experience.

study.title: Study Abroad
study.description: Students can spend part of their studies at a partner university abroad, experience a different academic environment, and earn credits recognized by their home university.

traineeship.title: Traineeships Abroad
traineeship.description: Students and recent graduates can gain practical work experience through international traineeships in companies, organizations, or institutions.

staff.title: Staff Mobility
staff.description: Academic and administrative staff can participate in teaching or training activities abroad, exchange knowledge, and strengthen international cooperation.

blended.title: Blended Mobility
blended.description: Participants can combine physical mobility abroad with online learning and collaborative activities, creating flexible international learning opportunities.

AboutPage.kutTitle: Erasmus+ at Kielce University of Technology
AboutPage.kutText: Kielce University of Technology actively participates in the Erasmus+ programme, providing opportunities for students and staff to take part in international mobility and cooperation with partner institutions.
AboutPage.charterText: The university holds the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education (ECHE) for the 2021–2027 programme period, supporting international cooperation and mobility in higher education.
AboutPage.documentsIntro: Explore important documents and policies related to Erasmus+ participation at Kielce University of Technology.
AboutPage.ctaText: Discover universities around the world that cooperate with Kielce University of Technology through Erasmus+.

outgoing.title: FOR KUT STUDENTS
outgoing.desc: Study or complete an internship abroad through Erasmus+ — here's how to get started.
outgoing.studies-desc: Spend one or two semesters studying at a partner university abroad. Courses taken there count towards your degree at KUT, agreed in advance through a Learning Agreement.
outgoing.intern-desc: Complete a work placement at a company, research centre or organisation abroad — from 2 to 12 months, including up to 12 months after graduation.
outgoing.short-desc: A compact alternative to a full exchange — blended intensive programmes and short doctoral mobility, combining a short physical stay with a virtual component.
outgoing.step-1: Check eligibility and choose a partner university
outgoing.step-2: Submit application to the recruitment committee
outgoing.p1: Currently enrolled KUT student (bachelor's, master's, or PhD).
outgoing.p2: Completed at least the first year of study.
outgoing.p3: Good academic standing, no outstanding disciplinary issues.
outgoing.p4: Basic proficiency in the language of instruction at the host institution.
outgoing.funding-desc: Erasmus+ grants cover part of your living and travel costs abroad, based on the destination country's cost-of-living group. Students with disabilities or from disadvantaged backgrounds can apply for top-up funding.
outgoing.ready-desc: Speak to your faculty coordinator about eligible partner universities and open calls.

incoming.title: FOR EXCHANGE STUDENTS
incoming.desc: Everything you need to plan, apply for, and complete an Erasmus+ exchange semester at Kielce University of Technology.
incoming.step-1-desc: Your home university nominates you to KUT through the inter-institutional agreement.
incoming.step-2-desc: Submit the application form, Learning Agreement, and required documents by the deadline.
incoming.step-3-desc: Receive your Letter of Acceptance and start planning accommodation and travel.
incoming.step-4-desc: Attend orientation week, register for courses, and get your student ID and residence documents.
incoming.p1: Get nominated by your home university's international office.
incoming.p2: Fill in the online application form and Learning Agreement.
incoming.p3: Submit your Erasmus+ Grant Agreement, transcript of records, and language certificate.
incoming.p4: Receive your Letter of Acceptance from KUT.
incoming.deadlines-desc: Nominations should reach the coordinator before the application deadline to allow time for course registration.
incoming.accomodation-desc: Rooms in KUT's student dormitories are reserved for incoming Erasmus+ students, close to the campus.
incoming.insurance-desc: EU/EEA students bring their EHIC; non-EU students must arrange private health insurance valid in Poland.
incoming.language-desc: Polish and English preparatory classes are offered before and during the semester.
incoming.ready-desc: Contact your home institution's international office to get nominated, then reach out to us with any questions.
